summary: The implementation preserves below-2-um technical-valid tracks in the primary biological population and confines their omission to an automatically reconciled specimen-level sensitivity scenario in technical QC. Short, long, wide, thin, curved/tortuous, low-ratio, fragmented-looking, fused-looking, and single-slice cases are handled without imposing WT morphology as the comparative acceptance target. Technical failures are based on unusable geometry or objective multi-object evidence, while unusual morphology remains measurable with warnings. Report artifacts correctly limit interpretation to sampled ROIs and make no group-effect claim. Biological identity of individual short tracks remains unresolved without independent manual or external validation, but the claim explicitly acknowledges that limitation.

findings.title: Individual short-track biological identity remains unresolved
findings.impact: The sensitivity analysis quantifies how below-2-um tracks affect specimen summaries, but it cannot establish whether any particular short track is a genuine nucleus, terminal optical section, unresolved fragment, or noise.
evidence: audits/claims_registry.json:179-180 states that length alone cannot distinguish a genuine short nucleus from an unresolved fragment.
audits/evidence/v571_rc6_candidate/report/02_quality_control/data/below_2_um_specimen_sensitivity.json:1-43 reports descriptive counts and medians rather than biological truth labels.
audits/validation/v571_6f9e73b_validation.md:93-94 states that the two representative specimens do not establish a biological group effect.
findings.recommendation: For claims about the biological identity or prevalence of short nuclei, obtain blinded independent manual instance masks across WT and mutant specimens and, where feasible, orthogonal imaging or external biological validation. Continue treating the present artifact as sensitivity analysis only.

limitations: Focused pytest execution could not start in the managed read-only environment because Python could not create a usable temporary directory. This review therefore relies on source inspection and the commit-retained validation receipt at audits/validation/v571_6f9e73b_validation.md:14-32.
No full image stack was run, as prohibited by the review instructions.
No other reviewers' outputs were read.
Only one included KJ specimen and one included WT specimen are represented in the retained sensitivity records; this supports execution and sensitivity transparency, not biological group inference.
No independent manual-mask or external biological ground truth establishes the identity of individual below-2-um tracks.
recommended_follow_up: Retain the below-2-um artifact exclusively under technical QC with its current descriptive-omission wording.
Before making a biological claim about genuine short-nucleus frequency, validate a blinded, specimen-stratified sample of short tracks against independent manual masks and raw Z context.
Use additional independent biological specimens before any WT-versus-mutant inference, with specimens—not tracks—as replicates.

If the audit coordinator needs a fresh test receipt for commit 22d29621230d31e2cf812ec28bec680d984ad2de, rerun the focused suite in a writable controlled temporary directory using the validated .venv.
